- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (especially 25–30d horizon) — add 2–3% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.  
- Forecast often lags 1–2 days in response to sentiment shifts — adjust by adding 0.5–1.0 point to forecast if sentiment rises sharply within last 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 0.8+ for 3+ days), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 10% below true peak if sentiment remains high.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment is strong.  
- For 30d horizon, avoid predicting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.2) over last 5 days.
